name: Tesla
description: Initially, many people saw the Tesla logo as simply a stylized “T,” without realizing there may be a deeper meaning behind it. Over time, there have also been some interesting theories floating around the web about what the “T” symbol might represent, including the idea that it resembles a cat’s nose. While those guesses have made the logo even more memorable, they are not the most widely accepted explanation. metaDescription: The Tesla logo is a sleek, stylized “T” based on the cross-section of an electric motor. The vertical part stands for a rotor pole, while the top bar represents a section of the stator.

name: Toyota
description: The Toyota brand takes its name from founder Kiichiro Toyoda. But the company wasn’t always called Toyota. When its automotive division first launched in 1933, it used the family name: Toyoda. In July 1936, the company held a public logo contest to mark its first passenger car and build visibility. Out of 27,000 submissions, a circular design featuring the Japanese characters for “Toyota” (トヨタ) won. The winning entry was a circular emblem, centering the word 'Toyota' written in sleek Japanese katakana characters (トヨタ). That winning design led the company to fully rebrand around the name Toyota
metaDescription: Toyota’s three-oval logo forms a hidden “T.” The inner ovals stand for trust between the brand and its drivers, while the outer oval represents the world and its global reach.

name: Honda
description: Honda’s a household name here in the States—you see their cars, bikes, and lawnmowers just about everywhere. But what a lot of folks don’t know is that it’s a classic Japanese surname, with deep ties to the country’s agricultural roots. Written in Japanese as 本田, the name breaks down into two characters: hon, which means "root," "origin," or "base," and da, which translates to "rice field." Way back in the Heian period (think 794 to 1185 AD), surnames were usually tied to the land—so "Honda" probably referred to someone who lived near the main rice fields in their village. Makes sense, right?
metaDescription: The Honda logo features a bold “H” for both the brand’s name and the founder’s initial, representing stability, confidence, and quality around the world.

name: BMW
description: The BMW "Roundel" is one of the most prestigious badges in automotive history. First hitting the scene in 1917, it’s survived over a century with its soul—and its signature blue-and-white colors—completely intact. But if you think you know the story behind those colors, you might be falling for one of the most successful marketing myths in history. The BMW "Roundel" is one of the most famous symbols in car history. metaDescription: The iconic blue and white of the BMW logo are inspired by Bavaria’s state flag. It serves as a permanent tribute to the company’s heritage and its birthplace in Munich, Germany.

name: Ford
description: In the car world, the Ford "Blue Oval" is as iconic as it gets. It’s been slapped on everything from the legendary Model T to the modern-day F-150, serving as a stamp of American industrial might for over a century. But where did it actually come from? Is that really Henry Ford’s signature on the grille, or just a clever bit of branding? There’s a long-standing myth in car circles that the Ford logo is a direct scan of Henry Ford’s own handwriting. metaDescription: The Ford logo shows the founder’s name in a smooth, flowing script. The classic blue stands for reliability and trust, and the oval shape reflects the brand’s global reach.

name: Subaru
description: In Japanese, “Subaru” (スバル) means “unite” or “gather together.” It’s a nice, low-key name that gets right to the brand’s heart—harmony and connection. But most people, don’t know there’s a starry backstory to it, too. Notice how the six stars are arranged in a pattern that closely mimics the actual Pleiades cluster shown here. The name wasn’t picked by chance—it’s a shout-out to the Pleiades star cluster, the group of stars that’s fascinated people for thousands of years.
